--- title: Footnote docs: - route: /docs/markdown title: Markdown - route: /docs/navigation-feedback title: Navigation Feedback --- Footnote turns GFM footnote markup (`[^1]` references and `[^1]: text` definitions) into dedicated Plate nodes you can insert, repair, and jump between. The reference is an inline void ``; the definition is a block at the end of the document. Paired with `MarkdownPlugin` and `remark-gfm`, references and definitions round-trip as real footnote markdown instead of fallback text. ## Features - GFM-compatible footnote references and definitions as dedicated Plate nodes. - One-transform insertion with automatic numeric ref allocation. - Typing `[^` opens a reference picker from the default UI kit. - Recreate a missing definition from an unresolved reference without duplicating. - Keep the first duplicate definition canonical; renumber later duplicates on demand. - Navigation helpers that jump between reference and definition with a landed-target flash. - HTML export and static pages link each reference to its note, and footnotes copied from GitHub paste as footnotes. - Pasted notes land at the end of the document, wherever the caret is. ## Kit usage ### Installation Use `FootnoteKit` for the reference and definition components and the `[^` picker. Add `MarkdownKit` for Markdown parsing and serialization. ### Add kit ```tsx import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; import { FootnoteKit } from '@/components/editor/footnote'; import { MarkdownKit } from '@/components/editor/markdown'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ // ...otherPlugins, ...FootnoteKit, ...MarkdownKit, ], }); ``` ## Manual usage ### Installation ```bash npm install platejs @tanstack/react-virtual marked remark-gfm remark-parse remark-stringify unified ``` ### Add plugins Add the inline reference and block definition. Pair the footnote plugins with `MarkdownPlugin` and `remark-gfm` so `[^1]` round-trips correctly. ```tsx import { FootnoteDefinitionPlugin, FootnotePlugin } from 'platejs/footnote/react'; import { MarkdownPlugin } from 'platejs/markdown'; import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; import remarkGfm from 'remark-gfm'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ // ...otherPlugins, FootnotePlugin, FootnoteDefinitionPlugin, MarkdownPlugin.configure({ initialState: { remarkPlugins: [remarkGfm], }, }), ], }); ``` Mount `FootnoteCombobox` in the plugin's `afterEditable` slot to open the picker when the reader types `[^`: ```tsx FootnotePlugin.configure({ slots: { afterEditable: FootnoteCombobox } }); ``` ### Insert a footnote Call `tx.footnote.insert` at the current selection. It inserts the reference, creates a matching definition at the end of the document, and moves the caret into the definition body so the reader can start writing: ```tsx editor.update((tx) => tx.footnote.insert()); ``` When the selection is expanded, the expanded fragment seeds the definition body so you can select text and "footnote-ify" it in one shot. Pass `focusDefinition: false` when the reference should stay inline (for example, inside a larger template): ```tsx editor.update((tx) => tx.footnote.insert({ focusDefinition: false })); ``` Pass `ref` to reuse an existing ref; the transform skips creating a duplicate definition when one already exists. ### Repair an unresolved reference When a reference points at a ref with no definition (e.g. pasted from elsewhere), use `tx.footnote.createDefinition` to create just the definition — without inserting another reference: ```tsx editor.update((tx) => tx.footnote.createDefinition({ ref: '3' })); ``` Pass `focus: false` when you want to leave the caret where it was: ```tsx editor.update((tx) => tx.footnote.createDefinition({ focus: false, ref: '3' }) ); ``` ### Navigate between reference and definition `editor.api.footnote.focusDefinition` and `editor.api.footnote.focusReference` scroll the target into view and flash it through [Navigation Feedback](/docs/plate/navigation-feedback). In an editable view they also move the selection to the target and focus the view. In a read-only view the selection and focus stay where they are. Call them from the mounted editor returned by `useEditor()`: ```tsx editor.api.footnote.focusDefinition({ ref: '3' }); editor.api.footnote.focusReference({ ref: '3' }); ``` When several references share a definition, pass `index` to choose a reference in document order: ```tsx editor.api.footnote.focusReference({ ref: '3', index: 1 }); ``` Both commands return `true` after navigating, and `false` for an unresolved target or an unmounted editor. For selection-only changes inside a transaction, use `tx.footnote.selectDefinition` or `tx.footnote.selectReference`; each returns the resolved `{ targetPath, point }` target or `null`. With `navigationFeedback: false`, footnote navigation still scrolls to the target, and selects and focuses it in an editable view, without a highlight. In a read-only view, the `FootnoteKit` components jump on a plain click or Enter. A reference jumps to its note. A note's back link jumps to its reference, or opens a picker of its citations when several references share the note; the arrow keys move through the picker and Enter jumps. After a jump, focus moves to the target's own jump control, so Enter jumps back. ### Handle duplicate definitions When definitions share a ref, the first definition in document order stays canonical; later ones are flagged as duplicates. Renumber a later duplicate with: ```tsx editor.update((tx) => tx.footnote.normalizeDuplicateDefinition({ path: duplicatePath, }) ); ``` The transform returns the newly assigned ref string on success, or `false` when the path isn't a duplicate definition or the requested ref is already taken. Pass `ref` to target a specific free ref instead of the next available one. ### Paste notes A pasted definition lands at the end of the document, after every block already there and before the empty paragraph `TrailingBlockPlugin` keeps. Its references and the rest of the paste land at the caret, in a table cell, a quote or a list item as in a paragraph, and the caret ends after the pasted text. One undo removes the whole paste. A definition saved inside another block stays there. Words copied from inside a note paste as words, without the note. A copy that covers a whole note keeps it, and a dragged note lands where it is dropped. ### Round-trip Markdown With `remark-gfm` configured, references serialize as `[^1]` and definitions as `[^1]: text`. Refs that Markdown would read as one label, such as `A` and `a`, are written as distinct labels. A reference whose definition is missing from the output reads back as text and reports a `markdown-unsupported-node` warning. ### Export and paste HTML `serializeHtml` writes each reference as a link to its note, and each note with a back link to its first reference: ```html 1

Source text

↩
``` The first reference to a ref gets the id `fnref-`, and the nth gets `fnref-:`. The note gets `fn-`, and a later duplicate gets `fn-:` with no back link. Each id percent-encodes the ref. Pasting the HTML back gives the same references and definitions without the back link. Footnotes copied from a page GitHub rendered, such as a README or a comment, paste as references and root definitions with the numbers GitHub shows. A citation pasted without its note becomes an unresolved reference. ### Static and Word output The `BaseFootnoteKit` static components draw each reference as a link to its note and give each canonical note a back link to its first reference, with the ids `editor.read.footnote.anchor` returns. A reference without a note links to the id its note would have. Word export writes the label and the note text without links. ### Customize rendering Swap in your own React components with `component`: ```tsx import { FootnoteDefinitionPlugin, FootnotePlugin } from 'platejs/footnote/react'; import { createEditor } from 'platejs/react'; const editor = createEditor({ plugins: [ FootnotePlugin.configure({ component: MyFootnoteReference }), FootnoteDefinitionPlugin.configure({ component: MyFootnoteDefinition }), ], }); ``` The package owns node semantics, ref allocation, and navigation helpers. App-level surfaces — hover previews, the `[^` combobox, slash-command entries, toolbar buttons — are built on top of the transforms and API methods below. ## Plugins ### `FootnotePlugin` Inline void node rendered as ``. Owns the `[^` trigger policy, ref registry, navigation transforms, and query API. Its state is a [ComboboxState](/docs/plate/combobox#comboboxstate). Text that opens the footnote picker. Completion replaces the whole `[^` and query, so `claim[^1` works after a word. - **Default:** `'[^'` Only trigger when the previous character matches. `null` allows any character. - **Default:** `null` Extra predicate gating the picker. Return `false` to keep a typed `[^` as text. ### `FootnoteDefinitionPlugin` Block node for footnote definitions. Lives at the bottom of the document and carries the ref + body content. ## Reads All read methods hang off `editor.read.footnote` and evaluate the active snapshot directly. ### `editor.read.footnote.definition` Get the first definition entry in document order for a ref. Footnote ref. Canonical definition entry, or `undefined` when nothing matches. ### `editor.read.footnote.definitions` Get every definition entry that shares a ref, in document order. When duplicates exist, the first entry is canonical; later entries are duplicates. Footnote ref. Definition entries in document order. ### `editor.read.footnote.definitionText` Get the plain-text content of the canonical definition. Ideal for hover previews — reads straight from live definition nodes, no copied state. Footnote ref. Definition text, or `undefined` when no definition exists. ### `editor.read.footnote.references` Get every reference entry that points at a ref, in document order. Footnote ref. Reference entries in document order. ### `editor.read.footnote.refs` List every ref that has at least one definition, in document order. Defined refs. ### `editor.read.footnote.nextRef` Compute the next free numeric ref. Used by `tx.footnote.insert` when the caller doesn't supply one. Next free ref (e.g. `'1'`, `'2'`). ### `editor.read.footnote.isResolved` Check whether a ref has at least one definition. Footnote ref. `true` when at least one definition exists for the ref. ### `editor.read.footnote.anchor` Get the fragment id of the footnote reference or definition at a path, and the id it links to. Static components and the HTML encoders use the same ids. Path of a footnote reference or definition. `{ id, target? }`, or `undefined` when no footnote is at `path`. A reference targets its note's id, even when the note is missing. A canonical definition targets its first reference, and a later duplicate has no `target`. ### `editor.read.footnote.isDuplicateDefinition` Check whether a given definition path is a later duplicate (not the canonical one). Path of the definition to check. `true` when the node at `path` is a footnote definition past the canonical one. ## Updates ### `editor.update.footnote.insert` Insert a footnote reference at the current selection, create a matching definition if one doesn't already exist, and focus the definition body. When the selection is expanded, the expanded fragment seeds the new definition body so you can convert selected prose into a footnote in one call. Reuse an existing ref. Defaults to `editor.read.footnote.nextRef()`. Focus the definition body after insertion. Pass `false` to keep the caret inline after the reference. Standard reference insertion options such as `at` and `select`. ### `editor.update.footnote.createDefinition` Create the missing definition for an existing ref without inserting another reference. Returns the path of the definition — the newly created one, or the existing one when the ref already resolves. Ref to create a definition for. Focus the definition body after creation. - **Default:** `true` Path of the resolved definition. ### `editor.api.footnote.focusDefinition` Scroll the canonical definition into view and flash it through Navigation Feedback. In an editable view, also move the selection into the definition body and focus the view. Footnote ref. `false` when the definition is missing or the calling view is unmounted; `true` after navigation, in an editable or a read-only view. ### `editor.api.footnote.focusReference` Scroll the matching reference into view and flash it through Navigation Feedback. In an editable view, also move the selection beside the reference and focus the view. Footnote ref. Pick a specific reference when the definition is pointed at by several. Indexed by document order. - **Default:** `0` `false` when the reference is missing or the calling view is unmounted; `true` after navigation, in an editable or a read-only view. ### `editor.update.footnote.normalizeDuplicateDefinition` Renumber a later duplicate definition so the canonical definition stays intact. Pass the path of the duplicate; optionally pass a specific `ref` to target, otherwise the transform picks `editor.read.footnote.nextRef()`. Path of the duplicate definition to renumber. Target ref. Must be free. Defaults to `editor.read.footnote.nextRef()`. The assigned ref on success, or `false` when the path isn't a duplicate definition or the target ref is already taken. ## Related docs - [Markdown](/docs/plate/markdown) - [Navigation Feedback](/docs/plate/navigation-feedback) - [Editor Methods](/docs/plate/editor-methods)
